guide.summary: Linear documents OAuth2 for applications that act for individual users, and the default user actor fits per-customer connections. The least-privilege documented grant for reading issues is the default read scope, which is included with every authorization.
guide.recommendation: The requested access is documented. Follow the saved setup steps and run each representative API test; execution has not been verified.

findings.title: Per-user OAuth2 authorization is documented
findings.detail: Linear documents an OAuth2 authorization-code flow for authorizing a user to the API, with a token exchange at the token endpoint. The actor parameter defaults to user, so each customer authorizes their own account.
findings.appliesWhen: Each individual customer account connects through its own OAuth authorization.

findings.title: read scope grants read access to the user's account

steps.title: Read the first page of issue titles
steps.detail: Send a POST to the GraphQL endpoint with the customer's OAuth access token in the Authorization Bearer header. The query requests the first 10 issues with includeArchived: true so archived issues are included, returning id and title in nodes plus pageInfo hasNextPage and endCursor. Read titles from data.issues.nodes[].title and the cursor fields from data.issues.pageInfo. Boundary check: the body contains only this issues query with no mutation, and no issueCreate or issueUpdate operation.
steps.doneWhen: The response has data.issues.nodes with title values and data.issues.pageInfo with hasNextPage and endCursor, and no errors array.

evidence.quote: # Pagination All list responses from queries return paginated results. We implement Relay style cursor-based pagination model with `first`/`after` and `last`/`before` pagination arguments. For example, this is how to query
#### Archived resources Archived resources are hidden by default from the paginated responses. They can be included by passing optional `includeArchived: true` as a query parameter for pagination.
``` Or pass the token as an authorization header: `Authorization: Bearer <ACCESS_TOKEN>`

request.example: curl 'https://api.linear.app/graphql' '-X' 'POST' '-H' 'Content-Type: application/json' '-H' 'Authorization: Bearer ACCESS_TOKEN' '--data' '{"query":"query { issues(first: 10, includeArchived: true) { nodes { id title } pageInfo { hasNextPage endCursor } } }"}'

fields: ACCESS_TOKEN: the customer's OAuth access token from the token exchange
data.issues.nodes[].title: the issue title scalar
data.issues.pageInfo.hasNextPage: true when another page exists
data.issues.pageInfo.endCursor: cursor for the next page

steps.title: Read each following page of issue titles until hasNextPage is false
steps.detail: Repeat the issues query with after set to the previous data.issues.pageInfo.endCursor, keeping first: 10 and includeArchived: true, and collect data.issues.nodes[].title from every page. Continue while data.issues.pageInfo.hasNextPage is true. Stop only when hasNextPage is false, which is the documented end of the collection. Use the returned endCursor unchanged and do not construct cursors. Boundary check: the request log must contain only these issues query POSTs and no mutation operations.
steps.doneWhen: Every page has been read in order by following endCursor, and pagination stops only when data.issues.pageInfo.hasNextPage is false, with no page skipped and no errors array in any response.

evidence.quote: } ``` To query the next 10, simply pass the value of `pageInfo.endCursor` as `after` parameter for the next request. You can do this as long as `pageInfo.hasNextPage` return true
and you'll paginate through all the values in the collection.
#### Archived resources Archived resources are hidden by default from the paginated responses. They can be included by passing optional `includeArchived: true` as a query parameter for pagination.

request.example: curl 'https://api.linear.app/graphql' '-X' 'POST' '-H' 'Content-Type: application/json' '-H' 'Authorization: Bearer ACCESS_TOKEN' '--data' '{"query":"query($after: String) { issues(first: 10, after: $after, includeArchived: true) { nodes { id title } pageInfo { hasNextPage endCursor } } }","variables":{"after":"END_CURSOR_FROM_PREVIOUS_PAGE"}}'

fields: END_CURSOR_FROM_PREVIOUS_PAGE: data.issues.pageInfo.endCursor from the prior response
ACCESS_TOKEN: the same customer's OAuth access token
